StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only scaling (MultiplayerScalingModel). Out of scope everywhere; the sim is single-player.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: Constant checked: FlutterPower.cs:24 declares `new DynamicVar("DamageDecrease", 50m)` and :36 returns it / 100m, i.e. 0.5 -- powers.py:2206. Dyadic, so outside hook_dispatch G9. `target != base.Owner -> 1m` matches powers.py:2205-2207.

AfterDamageReceived.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the stun's follow-up state is now taken from the last LOGGED state on the MonsterAi stream -- `machine.state_log[-1].get_next_state(self.owner, self.owner._move_rng)` (powers.py:2358-2364), where `_move_rng` is `combat.combat_rng.monster_ai` -- and handed to `CreatureCmd.stun` as `next_move_key`, mirroring FlutterPower.cs:47's `StateLog.Last().GetNextState(owner, RunRng.MonsterAi)`. The machine is no longer mutated by a `roll_move` call. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading powers.py:2308-2364. WAS: `machine.roll_move(self.owner, self.owner._rng)` drew off the monster's construction random.Random, never advanced MonsterAi, and walked the machine a turn early.

guards.rationale: powers.py:2217-2219 imports valueprops.is_powered_attack and tests `props` directly. This is the CORRECT form and is worth contrasting with SlowPower one file over, which tests the card instead.
powers.py:2222. The sim calls _expire() explicitly where C# leans on PowerCmd.Decrement -> ShouldRemoveDueToAmount; same observable, same note as the other units in this batch.
powers.py:2224-2225 guards with hasattr(self.owner, "is_hovering") instead of a cast. Defensive rather than divergent: the only applier is the hopper itself.
